text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'edge-proxy-prod' (PD#E23F7) — reason: multiple TLS handshake failures reported by ALB health checks and client telemetry. Paging @oncall-eng.

pagerduty: Trigger: edge-proxy-prod — High — TLS handshake failure rate > 10% across us-west-2 ALBs. Incident link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/E23F7

maria.k: acked on pager (maria.k) — taking initial triage. seeing 502/TLS handshake failures from synthetic probes and customer reports in us-west.

jin.h: on it, joining now. cc @samuel.t for networking. any deploys to certs or LB config in last 2 hours?

maria.k: we rotated certs for edge-proxy-prod at 01:10UTC for compliance — ATO certs pushed to ALB via automation. Automation reported success but I'm seeing a spike in TLS alerts ~01:20UTC. Could be cert chain mismatch or SNI.

samuel.t: checking ALB target groups and listeners. aws alb logs show TLS_alert_handshake_failure from clients, and target group health shows 1/3 healthy for tg-edge-usw2-01. healthcheck responses return 502 for app targets.

ops-bot: Deployed cert bundle v2026-03-14-0110 to ALB listeners: arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:... automation-run-id: run-4572. No errors in deploy job.

jin.h: pulling ALB listener config now. quick check: are we using SNI routing to multiple certs? could the cert we uploaded be missing SANs for certain custom domains?

maria.k: possible. list of affected customers coming from observability: customers with custom domains mapping to us-west endpoints — around 4 customers reporting TLS handshake errors and API timeouts. non-custom domain traffic (redwood.com/*) appears fine routed via global LB.

samuel.t: target instance logs show upstream handshake failing because the ALB terminates TLS; health checks to /_health are returning 502 with html error from nginx: 'upstream prematurely closed connection'. I suspect backend app healthchecks are failing after cert reload triggered an in-proc reload.

maria.k: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback cert rotation on US-WEST ALBs to previous cert; 2) shift Route53 weighted record to eu-central-1 to drain us-west; 3) restart app targets in target group to restore health checks. Thoughts?

jin.h: prefer minimal blast radius: roll back cert on ALB listener for us-west first. rollback command: 

aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn <listener> --certificates CertificateArn=<prev-cert-arn>

If that fails, start weight shift.

maria.k: executing rollback now on ALB listener arn:arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:listener/app/edge/50f6/abcd.

ops-bot: Listener modification request accepted. Change id: change-8891.

maria.k: rolling back...

maria.k: rollback applied. can folks confirm health checks?

samuel.t: healthchecks improving — tg-edge-usw2-01 now 3/3 healthy. ALB logs show TLS errors drop-off. Client error rate falling from 12% -> 1.2% in last 5m.

olivia.r: customer support: notified the four customers via priority channel, telling them we saw a cert rotation impact in us-west and are rolling back. will update with ETA for RCA.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by maria.k.

maria.k: temporary mitigation success: rollback restored healthy targets and reduced errors. however we should keep the incident open for root cause and follow-up: why did automation report success while cert bundle missing SANs for some custom domains? Also confirm whether cert deployed to some edge nodes but not others causing partial outage due to DNS cache.

jin.h: adding to timeline: 01:10UTC cert rotate automation run-4572; 01:20UTC increase in TLS handshake failures; 01:30UTC rollback applied; 01:45UTC client error rates normalized.

samuel.t: quick note: some DNS cache behavior amplified the impact. Custom domains with low TTLs resolved to us-west endpoints; after cert mismatch clients retried and some fell back to other regions once cached entries expired. TTLs of 300s meant partial propagation — but that reduced blast radius once caches cleared. Recording that for RCA.

maria.k: assigning owners: RCA owner = jin.h, follow-up: automation cert validation checks = samuel.t, customer comms = olivia.r.

jin.h: I'll investigate automation run logs and cert bundle contents. suspect our cert bundler removed intermediate CA or SAN for legacy custom domains. Also will add pre-deploy cert validation step to check SAN coverage and perform dry-run acceptance tests on a staging ALB.

maria.k: handing off to jin for long-running RCA. My oncall shift ends in 15m. Jin, please take incident command.

jin.h: taking command. ack handoff. next update by 02:15UTC or sooner if new developments.

olivia.r: posting interim customer update: "We experienced a partial TLS interruption affecting some custom domains in us-west due to a certificate rotation. We rolled back the change and service has recovered. Our engineering team is investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix."

pagerduty: Incident status: mitigated — trigger resolved by rollback action. Ticket PD#E23F7 moved to 'resolved' state at 02:00UTC by maria.k.

incident-bot: Created incident doc draft: /docs/incidents/2026-03-14-edge-cert-rotation-usw2.md — assign to jin.h for RCA.

jin.h: will produce RCA and include timeline, root cause, and follow-ups: 1) add cert bundle prevalidation; 2) update automation to fail deploy if SANs missing; 3) add canary sampling and synthetic checks post-deploy; 4) runbooks for certificate rollback.

maria.k: closing notes: customer impact limited to 4 customers in us-west, duration ~35 minutes for worst error window. No data loss. Thanks for fast ops. :thumbsup:

olivia.r: I'll follow-up with support ticket updates and a public status post if needed.

jin.h: last msg before I start RCA work — anyone see any other affected regions? I'll keep monitoring metrics and logs and will open a follow-up thread for the RCA.

samuel.t: nothing else flagged. marking network checks green.

maria.k: thanks team — handing off officially.
